The code is already written by the supervisor: `jsonpatch.mjs` (exports parsePointer, applyPatch, PatchError) and `jsonpatch-cli.mjs`. package.json has `"test": "node --test test/"` — put the tests in `test/` (e.g. test/jsonpatch.test.mjs and test/cli.test.mjs; CLI tests spawn `process.execPath` with temp files made via fs.mkdtempSync under os.tmpdir() and cleaned up). Ignore the `scratch/` dir (supervisor will delete it). Do not edit jsonpatch.mjs / jsonpatch-cli.mjs; if you find a spec violation, report it to me (main) in your REPORT with a failing test and the exact spec line — don't weaken the test.

Probe every spec line below with a test that a plausible wrong implementation would fail (e.g. inherited props like `toString`/`__proto__` counting as members, `01` accepted as index, `-` treated as bad index instead of not found, -0 lost on copy, member order wrong, hasOwn vs `in`, non-enumerable `op` member counted, String object path accepted, holes in patch, ops validated lazily instead of all up front, doc/patch mutated on failure, result sharing objects with value, move index counted before removal, copy into own child, test equality 0 vs -0 / 1 vs 1.0 / key order / array vs object, BOM handling, stdin byte counting, read order: doc not read until patch passes all checks (e.g. patch invalid JSON + doc missing → patch error), depth exactly 1000 OK vs 1001 too deep, '/dev/zero' style too large, directory, ENOTDIR path, usage cases incl. `-` alone and `- -` and 0/3 args).

FULL SPEC (authoritative):
<<<
Build a JSON Patch library `jsonpatch.mjs` (an ES module with the named exports `parsePointer`, `applyPatch` and `PatchError`) and a command-line tool `jsonpatch-cli.mjs` (run as `node jsonpatch-cli.mjs <patch> [<doc>]`). The rules follow JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) and JSON Patch (RFC 6902); where this text is more exact, this text wins. Throughout, a "string" is a primitive string; a String object such as `new String('/a')` is not a string.

Pointers
- A valid pointer is the empty string, or `/` followed by reference tokens separated by `/`: "" has no tokens, "/" has one token (the empty string), and "/a//b/" has the tokens "a", "", "b" and "".
- In a token, `~1` stands for `/` and `~0` for `~`, so "/~01" has the token "~1" and "/~10" has the token "/0". A `~` that is not followed by `0` or `1`, or a non-empty string that does not start with `/`, makes the pointer invalid.
- `parsePointer(pointer)` returns a new array of the decoded tokens. Not a string (String object included): TypeError `pointer must be a string`. Invalid: SyntaxError `invalid pointer`.
- A pointer is followed token by token, starting at the whole document:
  - On an object, a token names the object's own member of exactly that name, if it has one. `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString` etc are ordinary member names: inherited properties never count.
  - On an array, a token that is `0`, or a digit 1-9 followed by any digits, is an index: it names the element at that index when the index is less than the array's length. `-` names no element. Any other token (e.g. `01`, `+1`, `1.0`, `1e0`, ` 1`, `length` or "") is a bad index.
  - On a string, number, boolean or null, no token names anything.

Patches
- `applyPatch(doc, patch)` returns the document that results from applying `patch` to `doc`. `doc` is a JSON value as JSON.parse returns it. `patch`, each element and each member of an operation may be any JS value, except `value` of add/replace/test, when present, is a JSON value (never undefined). No getters/setters/Proxies. Docs/values ≤ 1000 levels deep.
- `applyPatch` never changes `doc` or `patch`, also when it throws, and the value it returns shares no object or array with them (a patch of `[]` returns a deep copy of `doc`). Every copy, including each `value` that add/replace/copy puts into the result, keeps every number exactly, -0 included (`[]` on `{"a":-0}` returns `{a: -0}`), and keeps member order.
- Member order is JS property order (Object.keys): array-index names first ascending, then others in insertion order. A new name goes last among names of its kind: adding `/1` with value 5 to `{"b":0}` gives `{"1":5,"b":0}`, and the CLI prints it in that order.
- `patch` must be an array (Array.isArray). Every index 0..length-1 holds an operation; a hole counts as undefined. First every operation is checked in order against the form rules; the first one breaking them stops applyPatch before anything is applied. Then ops applied in order; first failure stops.
- An operation has a member `name` when Object.hasOwn(op, name) is true, enumerable or not; inherited never count. Unused members are ignored whatever their value (`from` on add, `value` on remove).

Form rules (reason = first that applies)
- `not an object`: null, an array, or typeof not 'object' (function or hole → not an object; String object, Date go on).
- `bad op`: `op` missing or not === one of the strings add, remove, replace, move, copy, test.
- `bad path`: `path` missing, not a string, or invalid pointer.
- `bad from`: for move and copy, `from` missing, not a string, or invalid pointer.
- `missing value`: for add, replace, test, no `value` member (null is present).
- `cannot remove root`: remove with path "".
- `cannot move into own child`: move whose from tokens are a proper prefix of path tokens. from "" is a proper prefix of every other path; `/a` is not a prefix of `/ab`.

Operations
- add: path "" makes value the whole doc. Else follow tokens but last to parent. Object: missing name becomes new own member (placed per order rule), existing member gets value and keeps its place. Array: `-` appends, index ≤ length inserts at index shifting later elements up.
- remove: path must name a value, removed (array elements shift down).
- replace: path "" makes value the whole doc. Else path must name a value, which becomes value; member keeps its place.
- move: from must name a value. Removed as remove does, then added at path as add does, so an array index in path counts after the removal. from equal to path leaves the doc as is (once from is found).
- copy: from must name a value. A deep copy taken before anything changes is added at path as add does; path may lie inside from.
- test: path must name a value ("" names whole doc), equal to value: same JSON type, numbers same value (1, 1.0, 1e0 equal; 0 and -0 equal); strings exactly same chars (no normalization); arrays same length and equal elements in order; objects same member names any order with equal values; true/false/null equal only themselves.

Failures while applying
- First token of a pointer that names nothing stops the op: `bad index` if a bad index on an array, else `from not found` while following from and `path not found` while following path. move and copy follow from first.
- add follows only the parent; its last token fails with `path not found` when the parent is neither object nor array, or is an array and the token is an index > length, and `bad index` when parent is array and token is neither `-` nor an index.
- `test failed`: value at path does not equal value.

Errors
- PatchError subclass of Error, name 'PatchError', has `index`. applyPatch throws nothing else.
- patch not an array: message `patch must be an array`, index null. Else `operation <i>: <reason>`, index = number i.

Command line
- `node jsonpatch-cli.mjs <patch> [<doc>]` reads patch from file <patch> and doc from file <doc>. Missing <doc>, or an argument exactly `-`, means stdin.
- Success: write JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) + "\n" to stdout, nothing to stderr, exit 0.
- Inputs read as UTF-8; a BOM at the very start is ignored. Then parsed as JSON.parse.
- Order: arguments; patch input (read, decode, parse, depth check); doc input (same four); applying. Doc input not read until patch input passed every check.
Errors (exactly one line to stderr ending "\n"; nothing to stdout). <name> is the argument as given, or `stdin`.
- Not 1 or 2 args, or both inputs stdin: `Usage: node jsonpatch-cli.mjs <patch> [<doc>]`, exit 2.
- Read errors exit 1, first that applies: `Error: <name>: no such file` (ENOENT or ENOTDIR, e.g. `nope.json` or `patch.json/x` where patch.json is a regular file). `Error: <name>: is a directory` (whatever its permissions). `Error: <name>: too large`: more than 1048576 bytes (BOM included) actually read. `Error: <name>: cannot read`: any other read error. For stdin only too large and cannot read apply.
- Invalid UTF-8: `Error: <name>: invalid UTF-8`. JSON.parse rejects (empty included): `Error: <name>: invalid JSON`. Nested more than 1000 levels: `Error: <name>: too deep` (primitives depth 0; [] and {} depth 1). Each exit 3.
- applyPatch throws PatchError: `Error: <message>`, exit 4.
>>>

Done means: `npm test` (node --test test/) passes in the project root, tests cover each spec line above, and any spec violation you found in the implementation is listed in your REPORT with the failing case. No other builder sections are awake. End with your REPORT block.
